entries.title: I Timothy 1:2
segments: Unto Timothy. Then preaching at Ephesus.  The epistle seems to have been written to afford Timothy documentary proof that Paul endorsed his teachings.

entries.title: I Timothy 1:3
segments: Ephesus.  The chief city of Asia Minor and one of the 'free' cities under the Roman empire.  Here was the celebrated temple of the goddess Diana, to whose worship they city, as a whole, was devoted.  See

.
 

 
Macedonia. The northern Roman province of Greece, the southern being Achaia.  Its chief city was Philippi.  See

entries.title: I Timothy 1:4
segments: Fables. Fanciful traditions as to the origin of angels and their powers, and similar superstitions.  See

.
 

 
 Genealogies...questionings. Fruitless speculation on things of no importance. The one vital matter was faith in Christ Jesus.

entries.title: I Timothy 1:7
segments: Of the law. From the context this is accepted as being the Mosaic law, which the Judaizers were trying to impose upon the Ephesian church.
